fightLines.line: 🪤 Your old life comes back to your hands: the pit you dug before the Scattering — deep enough for a boar, staked at the bottom, brushed over with leaves and marked well. You never forgot the shape of it.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Regina Becker. Trail crew lead. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Daughter's Drawing, Trail compass, Seed packet, Tote Bag, Carpenter's square. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. Last night, something walked past the treeline on two legs. Too tall. It stopped. It listened. Then it kept going. Nobody slept after that.
You remember the Kitchen knife at your space in the haven and fetch it — it rides in your pack now.
